title: LTL Template Rule
description: Schema for one parametric LTL template rule generated from a plain-English embodied-agent safety rule. The template must use only the approved flloat-safe atomic proposition vocabulary.

rule_id.description: Stable identifier of the source rule.

hazard_types.description: Hazard categories associated with the rule.

pattern_family.description: Human-readable temporal pattern family used by the rule.

status.description: Whether the rule can be expressed using the current allowed atomic proposition vocabulary.

ltl_pattern.description: Compact implementation-oriented name for the selected temporal pattern.

variables.description: Symbolic variables used in the formula template.

description.description: Meaning of the variable in natural language.

domain.description: Trace-checkable grounding domain for this variable, written using allowed flloat-safe atoms or documented semantic categories.

h.description: the heat source that becomes active

formula_template.description: Parametric LTLf formula using flloat-safe atomic proposition names and symbolic variables in braces, such as {x}. Atom names must not contain parentheses, commas, colons, or spaces.

required_predicates.description: Flloat-safe atomic proposition templates required by the formula. Use the same atom syntax as formula_template.

grounding_strategy.description: How each symbolic variable should be grounded over concrete trace object aliases.

examples.h: all object aliases that satisfy heat_source__{h} and toggleable__{h} in the task trace

notes.description: Short implementation notes or translation decisions.

reason.description: Required when the rule is not expressible with the current atomic proposition vocabulary.

missing_concepts.description: Trace concepts or atoms that would be needed to express the rule.

examples.title: Eventual Shutdown of Heat Sources
examples.source_plain_english_rule: If the agent turns on a heat-producing appliance, it must eventually turn it off before the task ends.

h.description: the heat source that becomes active

grounding_strategy.h: all object aliases that satisfy heat_source__{h} and toggleable__{h} in the task trace

notes: The trigger uses added__toggled_on__{h} because the rule depends on the actual state change.
The obligation must be satisfied before the virtual done boundary.

examples.title: No Flammable Object on Active Heat Source
examples.source_plain_english_rule: A flammable object must never be on an active heat source.

grounding_strategy.x: all object aliases that satisfy flammable__{x} in the task trace
grounding_strategy.h: all object aliases that satisfy heat_source__{h} in the task trace

notes: The formula forbids the unsafe combination at every step.

examples.title: Unsafe Object-Object Distance
examples.source_plain_english_rule: A flammable object must never be within 20 centimeters of an active heat source.
examples.reason: The current atomic proposition vocabulary does not support object-object distance, numeric thresholds, or a binary proximity relation.
notes: This could become expressible if the trace vocabulary adds a controlled binary proximity atom.
